findings.reason: as written the node's first assertion passes before and after the change and the declared control cannot make it red, so the half of §52 that deletes `_figure_row` is gated by a check that proves nothing; measuring the field *union* (every key `figure_rows` yields agrees, which is red today because the index row carries none of `caption`, `dims`, `download`, `for_plan`, `path`) would fail on the unfixed code and pass only once the index reads through `figure_rows`.
findings.text: §52's first done-when item ("the index's figure row and `figure_rows`' row for the same path agree on every shared key") already holds on the unfixed code, and the control it declares for it ("keep `metadata_index._figure_row` deriving the index row on its own, and the agreement case fails on the keys the two rows do not share") is false in both halves — the two rows share exactly `href`, `slug`, `title`, `type`, all four already derived identically on the current code, and an assertion over *shared* keys cannot fail on keys the rows *do not share* — measured on all 535 figures under `docs/figures`, the index row and the `figure_rows` row disagree on 0 shared keys while each row carries 8 and 5 keys the other lacks (`index-only: archived, created, edited, height, revision, sprint, status, width`; `figures-only: caption, dims, download, for_plan, path`), so the item measures the field *intersection*, which the fix merges only because both sides already build it the same way

findings.reason: the equality assertion is red only when the two calls straddle a midnight (the plan's own rule against a test that encodes the current date), so the node either ships a date-fused flake onto the primary branch or cannot judge its own item; the measure should compare a normalised projection of the payload, or pin the moment the payload reads.
findings.text: §50's first done-when item requires that a second roadmap call with nothing changed "returns a result equal to the first", but the roadmap payload is not time-stable: `reckon/roadmap.py:3978-3984` attaches `age_days` from `_authorisation_age` → `doccheck.derived_plan_age`, whose reference day is `date.today()` (`reckon/doccheck.py:308`).
